safi-cedvel:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) is an adverbial of condition in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis تحدّث [Note: or to (يصدر) الناس.], (زلزالها) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.
Clause: «زلزلت الأرض ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Verses 2-5: (الواو) is a conjunction in both places (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (لها) is attached to an omitted khabar of ما, (يومئذ) is an adverb of time, accusative — or indeclinable — annexed to a temporal noun, attached to the answer of إذا, and so it is a badal of it; and the tanwīn in (إذ) is a substitute for something omitted, i.e. "the day when the earth is shaken ... it will tell" (لها) is attached to (أوحى) [Note: the verb أوحى is transitivized by (إلى): «قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ ...». The apparent sense is that the one inspired is omitted, namely the angels, i.e.: your Lord inspired the angels for the sake of the earth, i.e. for the sake of what its inhabitants do on it; it is also possible to have أوحى include the meaning of "permitted", i.e.: He permitted it to tell.].
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ربّك أوحى..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (تحدّث).
And the clause: «أخرجت الأرض ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause زلزلت.
And the clause: «قال الإنسان ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause زلزلت.
And the clause: «ما لها ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «تحدّث أخبارها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «أوحى لها ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.
Verse 6: (يومئذ) is an emphasis of the first [Note: or attached to (يصدر).], (أشتاتا) is an accusative ḥāl from الناس (اللام) is for causation (يروا) is an accusative imperfect by an implied أن after the lām, and the wāw in (يروا) is the nāʾib fāʿil, and in (أعمالهم) a muḍāf is omitted, i.e. "the recompense of their deeds"..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يروا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يصدر).
And the clause: «يصدر الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution: in His saying, the Exalted «إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزالَها وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقالَها».
The bringing out is attributed to the earth figuratively, because the true bringer out is Allah, Glory be to Him, the Exalted, and the earth is the place of the bringing out.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿ) (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (خيرا) is an accusative tamyīz [Note: or a badal of مثقال, accusative.] ..
Clause: «من يعمل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يصدر الناس [Note: in verse (6) of the sūra.].
And the clause: «يعمل ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is possible that the khabar is the two clauses, of condition and answer, together.].
And the clause: «يره» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
Verse 8: (الواو) is a conjunction (من يعمل ... يره) is like the first, in words and clauses.

* Benefits:
- The unique comprehensive verse:
It is said that this verse was revealed concerning two men. When (وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعامَ عَلى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِيناً وَيَتِيماً وَأَسِيراً) was revealed, one of them, when the beggar came to him, would think it too little to feed him a date, a morsel of bread, a walnut and the like, and would say: "This is nothing for which one is rewarded; we are rewarded only for what is given while we love it." And the other would make light of a small sin like a lie or a glance and the like, and say: "Allah promised the Fire only for the major sins, and there is no sin in this." So Allah revealed (فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ): He, Glory be to Him, the Exalted, urges them to do even a little good, for it is about to become much, and warns them against the small sin, for it is about to become great. Ibn Masʿūd said: "The most decisive verse in the Qur'an is this verse."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called this verse "the unique comprehensive one" (al-jāmiʿa al-fādhdha) when he was asked about the zakat on donkeys, and said: "Allah has revealed nothing about them except this unique comprehensive verse."
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them both, each gave in charity a single grape, and said: "How many weights of ants (dharra) are in it!" The aim of that was to teach others, otherwise the two were among the generous of the Companions. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym said: A man passed by al-Ḥasan while he was reciting this sūra, and when he reached its end he said: "Allah is sufficient for me; the admonition has been completed."
- Some rulings on the tamyīz:
The tamyīz is of two kinds:
A- Tamyīz of a single word (tamyīz mufrad): that whose specified item is pronounced and indicates:
1- A number: such as: (فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة).
2- A weight: such as: (اشتريت رطلا عسلا) ("I bought a pound of honey").
3- A measure of capacity: such as: (بعتك صاعا تمرا) ("I sold you a ṣāʿ of dates").
4- An area: such as: (زرعت هكتارا أرضا) ("I planted a hectare of land").
5- A measure of length: such as: (سرت عشرين مترا) ("I walked twenty metres").
In this kind it is permissible for the tamyīz to be accusative, as in the preceding examples, or genitive by min, such as: (اشتريت صاعا من تمر) ("I bought a ṣāʿ of dates"), or genitive by annexation, such as: (اشتريت صاع تمر). As for the tamyīz of number, it comes singular and accusative with the numbers from eleven to nineteen, as in His saying, the Exalted: (إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً) (فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً) and (هذا أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً). It comes plural and genitive with the numbers from three to ten, as in His saying, the Exalted: (سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وَثَمانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً). And it comes singular and genitive with a hundred, a thousand and a million, as in His saying, the Exalted: (بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عامٍ) (فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عاماً).
B- Tamyīz of a sentence (tamyīz jumla): that whose specified item is noticed and understood from the meaning of the sentence. This kind always comes accusative, as in His saying, the Exalted: (وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُوناً) (وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْباً) (فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْساً) (أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَراً).
